cases.question: What does chronic absenteeism actually mean and how is it measured?
shown: California defines a chronic absentee as: 'a pupil who is absent on 10 percent or more of the schooldays in the school year when the total number of days a pupil is absent is divided by the total number of days the pupil is enrolled and school was actually taught in the regular day schools of the district, exclusive of Saturdays and Sundays.'

The chronic absenteeism rate is calculated as: 'The unduplicated count of students determined to be chronically absent (Chronic Absenteeism Count) divided by the Chronic Absenteeism Enrollment at the selected entity for the selected population using the available filters.'

Not every enrolled student is counted in the eligible enrollment. The state removes students 'that were not eligible to be considered chronically absent at that entity. Students that are expected to attend less than 31 instructional days at the selected entity or who were enrolled but did not attend the selected entity are not eligible to be considered chronically absent at that entity.'
A day attended is defined broadly: 'A day attended is defined as any day a student attended for all or part of a school day.'

The data itself comes from schools and districts: 'Absenteeism data are submitted by local educational agencies (LEAs) and charter schools to the California Department of Education (CDE) as part of the annual End of Year 3 (EOY 3) data submission in the California Longitudinal Pupil Achievement Data System (CALPADS).'

withheld_claims.text: To protect student privacy, some figures in the data files may be withheld: 'data are suppressed (*) on the Chronic Absenteeism downloadable files if the cell size within a selected student population (Chronic Absenteeism Eligible Cumulative Enrollment) is 10 or less.'

cases.question: What is Census Day?
shown: Census Day is defined as the first Wednesday in October.
It is the single day used to take the official annual count of enrolled students.

The counts from Census Day are calculated at each level — state, county, district, and school — and are considered distinct, unduplicated counts that are additive from one reporting level to the next.

The Census Day data are submitted by local educational agencies and charter schools to the California Department of Education as part of the annual Fall 1 data submission, and must be certified as accurate by district superintendents, charter school administrators, or their designees.

cases.question: ¿Qué significa ausentismo crónico y cómo se mide?
shown: La ley de California define a un 'estudiante crónicamente ausente' como aquel que estuvo ausente el 10% o más de los días escolares en el año, calculado dividiendo el total de días de ausencia entre el total de días en que el estudiante estuvo matriculado y se impartió clases, excluyendo sábados y domingos.
La tasa de ausentismo crónico se calcula dividiendo el número de estudiantes crónicamente ausentes entre la matrícula acumulada elegible de la escuela o entidad seleccionada.

No todos los estudiantes matriculados son elegibles para este cálculo: se excluyen quienes se espera que asistan menos de 31 días instructivos, quienes estuvieron matriculados pero no asistieron, y quienes tienen estado de exención (por ejemplo, estudiantes en escuelas no públicas o en instrucción en casa u hospital).
Para el año escolar 2024-25, la tasa de ausentismo crónico de todos los estudiantes en Birch Lane Elementary fue de 16.9%.
